newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Philips' Elekta stake not above 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philips' Elekta stake not above 10 pct.

text.p: Philips Electronics N.V. will take a shareholding no greater than 10 percent in Elekta AB of Sweden under a proposed deal to merge the two companies' radiation therapy activities, Elekta spokesman Sverker Littorin told Reuters.
Earlier on Thursday, Philips Medical Systems International B.V. and Elekta said they were discussing merging Philips' radiation therapy activities with Elekta's under the control of Elekta.
Under the proposed deal, a new organisation based in Crawley, England, will provide the medical community with products, information and support in the radiation therapy field.

The proposed merger will be financed by banks and a new issue placement directed at Philips, but Elekta's managing director Laurent Leksell said in statement this should not result in any deterioration of Elekta's earnings per share.
A stake of 10 percent would make Philips the second largest shareholder in Elekta after the Leksell family.
"We agreed not to say how big the transaction is in crowns. But we do not expect Philips to acquire more than 10 percent of shares in Elekta," Littorin said.
The Swedish news agency TT said the transaction could more than double Elekta's annual turnover to two billion crowns from the present 800 million.
This would make the Swedish company one of the world's biggest suppliers of cancer treatment equipment. -- Tony Austin, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1017
